issues.description: Method signature mismatch for acceptSupplyDelivery: problem_statement.md (UML and descriptive text) documents acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity) while the code example in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java calls acceptSupplyDelivery("Bacon", 50, 100) (three arguments) and the reference implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java declares public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (three parameters: ingredientName, price, quantity). This discrepancy leaves students unsure which parameter list to implement and may cause compilation errors or inconsistent example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the acceptSupplyDelivery signature across artifacts. Preferred quick fix: update the problem statement UML and descriptive text to specify the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) so it matches the template example and the reference solution. Alternative: change the template Main.java and the reference solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all example calls to pass a supplier name. Ensure the UML, textual description, example calls, and reference implementation all match after the change.
